about: Reference fixture for online FDR (LORD++, SAFFRON) in backend/research_ledger.py (ROADMAP 2.12). Published cases are parsed from onlineFDR's own rendered example output; every printed alpha_i matches ref.py to within half a unit in the last printed digit, and every printed R_i matches exactly.

conventions.indexing: t is 1-based; expected_rejections_1based lists t with R_t = 1
conventions.reject_rule: R_t = 1 iff p_t <= alpha_t (onlineFDR); the papers' code uses p_t < alpha_t
conventions.lord_gamma: gamma_j = c*log(max(j,2))/(j*exp(sqrt(log(j)))), c = gamma_c, not renormalised to a horizon
conventions.saffron_gamma: gamma_j = 0.4374901658 / j^1.6 (= j^-1.6 / zeta(1.6)), not renormalised to a horizon
conventions.tolerance: alpha_abs_tol[i] is half a unit in the last digit R printed for alpha_i
conventions.lord_wealth: W(0)=w0; W(t)=W(t-1)-alpha_t+R_t*b_t; b_t=alpha-w0 until the first rejection, alpha after
conventions.saffron_wealth: W(0)=(1-lambda)*w0; W(t)=W(t-1)-(1-C_t)*alpha_t+R_t*(1-lambda)*b_t, C_t=1{p_t<=lambda}, b_t=alpha-w0 at the first rejection, alpha after (diagnostic, not used by alpha_t)

source.note: p-values are vignettes/advanced-usage.Rmd sample.df reordered by the set.seed(1) within-date permutation printed (as ids) in the LORD help page example set.seed(1); LORD(sample.df, alpha=0.1, w0=0.05); R is not printed, so expected_R comes from p_t <= printed alpha_t
